findings.claim: Across the full observed score window (0.0-0.49, 50 nodes, 14 independent batches), landmark_00_soft_mass shows a strong early positive rate (first_rate_z ~ +9.3) that reverses to a strong negative late rate (last_rate_z ~ -10.0), with 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict; the whole-window level z is small (~0.64) and no polynomial was accepted (relative node RMSE ~0.29). This is a changing contrast, not a stationary target.

landmark_00_local_dy has the largest early rate magnitude (first_rate_z ~ -72.4) decaying to a small late rate (last_rate_z ~ +5.5) with 6 sign changes and 4 strong sign conflicts; whole-window level z is small (~-0.30). The rate contrast is large but the level is near-flat over the window.

landmark_00_local_dx shows a strong negative early rate (first_rate_z ~ -17.5) reversing to positive late rate (last_rate_z ~ +8.1) with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts; whole-window level z is small (~-0.18).

landmark_00_local_cxy has the largest early positive rate (first_rate_z ~ +64.8) reversing to negative late rate (last_rate_z ~ -19.7) with 9 sign changes and 14 strong sign conflicts; whole-window level z is near zero (~0.10).

landmark_00_local_cyy shows a strong negative early rate (first_rate_z ~ -36.5) reversing to positive late rate (last_rate_z ~ +17.1) with 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict; whole-window level z is small (~-0.58).

landmark_00_local_czz shows a positive early rate (first_rate_z ~ +15.2) reversing to negative late rate (last_rate_z ~ -6.3) with 7 sign changes and 6 strong sign conflicts; whole-window level z is small (~-0.31).

landmark_00_local_dz shows a positive early rate (first_rate_z ~ +14.1) reversing to a small negative late rate (last_rate_z ~ -2.4) with 10 sign changes and 7 strong sign conflicts; whole-window level z is near zero (~-0.02).

landmark_00_local_cxx shows a negative early rate (first_rate_z ~ -7.9) reversing to positive late rate (last_rate_z ~ +15.9) with 6 sign changes and 2 strong sign conflicts; whole-window level z is small (~-0.58).
landmark_00_local_cxz shows small same-sign early and late rates (first_rate_z ~ +8.8, last_rate_z ~ +10.0) with 7 sign changes and 2 strong sign conflicts; whole-window level z is near zero (~0.14).

landmark_00_local_cyz shows a negative early rate (first_rate_z ~ -16.4) reversing to positive late rate (last_rate_z ~ +8.9) with 7 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts; whole-window level z is small (~-0.25).

hypotheses.direction: early positive rate, late negative rate; whole-window level near reference
hypotheses.falsifier: If the landmark_00_soft_mass rate does not reverse sign between early and late observed nodes, or if the whole-window level departs strongly from its reference, the proposed early-robust/late-baseline curvature ramp is not supported.
hypotheses.scope: global over the full observed score window [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_soft_mass coordinate exhibits a sign-reversing temporal contrast over the observed score window: a positive early rate that becomes a strong negative late rate, while the whole-window level remains near its reference. A reward schedule that ramps curvature from a robust early response toward baseline late (as in the registered C1-style delta ramp) would align with this observed early-to-late rate reversal.

hypotheses.direction: large early rate magnitude decaying to small late rate; near-flat whole-window level
hypotheses.falsifier: If the landmark_00_local_dy early rate magnitude is not substantially larger than its late rate magnitude, or if the whole-window level shows a strong monotone drift, the transient early-contrast hypothesis fails.
hypotheses.scope: global over the full observed score window [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_dy coordinate shows a large-magnitude early rate that decays toward a small late rate with multiple sign changes, indicating a transient early contrast rather than a sustained directional drift. A reward that applies stronger early curvature (larger delta early) and relaxes later would match this transient profile.

hypotheses.direction: large early positive rate reversing to negative late rate; near-zero whole-window level
hypotheses.falsifier: If the landmark_00_local_cxy rate does not reverse sign between early and late nodes, or if a constant-curvature schedule reproduces the same observed rate profile, the time-varying curvature hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.scope: global over the full observed score window [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_cxy coordinate has the largest early positive rate among landmark_00 features, reversing to a strong negative late rate with many sign changes and strong sign conflicts, indicating a highly non-stationary contrast. This supports a time-varying curvature schedule rather than a constant-curvature control.

hypotheses.direction: negative early rate, positive late rate; small whole-window level
hypotheses.falsifier: If the landmark_00_local_cyy rate does not reverse sign between early and late nodes, the early-to-late contrast reversal hypothesis fails.
hypotheses.scope: global over the full observed score window [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_cyy coordinate shows a strong negative early rate reversing to a positive late rate, consistent with an early-to-late contrast reversal similar to landmark_00_soft_mass but with opposite early sign. A curvature schedule that is robust early and baseline late would produce a different early response for this coordinate than a baseline-early/robust-late schedule.

hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_cxz coordinate shows small same-sign early and late rates with several sign changes, indicating a weak or near-stationary contrast over the window. This coordinate provides limited evidence for a time-varying curvature schedule.

hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_cyz coordinate shows a negative early rate reversing to a positive late rate with several strong sign conflicts, indicating a non-stationary contrast. A time-varying curvature schedule would be more consistent with this profile than a constant-curvature control.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curve features and trend summaries were inspected.
No decoded final affinity labels are present in the role input; selection preference and rate contrasts are associations, not measured final benefit.
The observed rate contrasts are derived from predicted endpoint world A features and do not by themselves specify an absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient.
Several features show many sign changes and strong sign conflicts, so the early/late rate reversal is a summary of a noisy non-monotone profile rather than a clean two-phase trend.
No polynomial was accepted for the inspected landmark_00 features, so the reported rates are observed-node linear summaries, not validated polynomial fits.
The registered temporal recipes (C1, C2, C3) are proposed interventions, not parameters learned from the observed temporal slopes.
